title: Schedule the production release
instruction:
# Schedule the production release

Use the **Northstar Release Desk** in the browser to review all four release
candidates and schedule the one candidate that satisfies every production rule:

- no open severity-1 incidents;
- regression pass rate of at least 97%;
- both Security and QA approvals;
- rollback rehearsal completed;
- the maintenance window must be in the EU-West region.

Open candidate details as needed; the summary cards do not contain every fact.
For the unique eligible candidate, open its scheduling form and set:

- change owner: `Mira Chen`
- acknowledgement: confirm that the rollback lead has been notified
- deployment note: `Proceed after final telemetry snapshot`

Submit the schedule and leave the application showing its confirmation. Do not
schedule an ineligible candidate.

files.text:
FROM <base-image>

RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends sqlite3 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /workspace

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

: "${TASK_PUBLIC:?TASK_PUBLIC is required}"
mkdir -p /workspace/notes
/usr/bin/sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/harbor-run-service \
  "$TASK_PUBLIC/release_desk.py" > /workspace/notes/release-desk.log 2>&1 &

for attempt in $(seq 1 80); do
  page="$(/usr/bin/python3 - <<'PY' 2>/dev/null || true
import urllib.request
print(urllib.request.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:8099/health", timeout=0.4).read().decode())
PY
)"
  if [ "$page" = "northstar-release-desk:ready" ]; then exit 0; fi
  sleep 0.25
done

echo "Northstar Release Desk did not become ready on port 8099" >&2
if [ -r /workspace/notes/release-desk.log ]; then tail -40 /workspace/notes/release-desk.log >&2; fi
exit 1

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

script_path="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$script_path"' EXIT
printf '%s\n' '[
  {"action":"read_page"},
  {"action":"click","selector":"#candidate-borealis"},
  {"action":"read_page"},
  {"action":"click","selector":"#back-to-board"},
  {"action":"click","selector":"#candidate-cascade"},
  {"action":"read_page"},
  {"action":"click","selector":"#back-to-board"},
  {"action":"click","selector":"#candidate-atlas"},
  {"action":"read_page"},
  {"action":"click","selector":"#schedule-atlas"},
  {"action":"type_text","selector":"#owner","text":"Mira Chen"},
  {"action":"click","selector":"#rollback-ack"},
  {"action":"type_text","selector":"#deployment-note","text":"Proceed after final telemetry snapshot"},
  {"action":"click","selector":"#confirm-schedule"},
  {"action":"read_page"}
]' > "$script_path"
/usr/bin/sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/harbor-browser-mcp.py run --script "$script_path"

#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail

reward=0
db=/var/lib/harbor-service/release-desk.db
public_app=/opt/harbor-authored/public/release_desk.py
expected_hash=87c47c616fedb1aaa4ffc4cebd9d710be995a62ae50c4cd390e5a9952440196d
mkdir -p /logs/verifier

if [ -r "$public_app" ] && [ "$(sha256sum "$public_app" | awk '{print $1}')" = "$expected_hash" ] && [ -r "$db" ]; then
  result="$(sqlite3 -separator '|' "$db" "SELECT candidate_id, owner, rollback_ack, deployment_note, status FROM schedules ORDER BY id;")"
  count="$(sqlite3 "$db" 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schedules;')"
  initial_count="$(sqlite3 "$db" 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM candidates;')"
  if [ "$count" = "1" ] && [ "$initial_count" = "4" ] && [ "$result" = 'atlas|Mira Chen|1|Proceed after final telemetry snapshot|scheduled' ]; then reward=1; fi
fi

printf '%s\n' "$reward" > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
printf 'reward=%s\n' "$reward"
exit 0

notes:
# Northstar Release Desk task

The agent uses a local Chrome application to inspect four release candidates,
apply a multi-criterion production policy, and submit scheduling details for the
unique eligible candidate. See [instruction.md](instruction.md).

## Environment

The task builds from the pinned `browser-chrome-v1` image and installs the
SQLite CLI. A standard-library Python service owns a SQLite database under
`/var/lib/harbor-service` and serves the application on loopback port 8099. The
agent has 2 CPUs, 2 GiB RAM, 4 GiB storage, no runtime network, and 600 seconds.
Setup launches the service as the protected `appsvc` account.

## Verifier

The custom deterministic verifier checks the service-owned SQLite state. Full
credit requires exactly one schedule with the correct candidate, owner,
acknowledgement, note, and status. It also checks that all four source records
remain and that the staged application asset has its authored SHA-256 digest.
The reward is binary (`0` or `1`).

## Layout

```
.
├── instruction.md                 Agent-facing workflow
├── task.toml                      Runtime and MCP declaration
├── environment/
│   ├── Dockerfile                 Pinned image plus SQLite CLI
│   ├── setup.sh                   Protected-service launcher/readiness
│   └── public/release_desk.py     Local application and initial data
├── solution/solve.sh              Oracle browser trajectory
└── tests/test.sh                  Server-state verifier
```

## Running

```bash
harbor run -p output/env_000 -a oracle
harbor run -p output/env_000 -a terminus-2
```
